purpose: Discover and split 女X entities across the 508GB corpus while separating deity/person, ritual person, genealogy, place, grammar, reading variants, state/clan hypotheses, and unresolved nodes before any cultural-family or sex inference.
epistemic_rule: Exact strings are retrieval seeds only. 女+core graph is cross-tradition; 女 may participate in sex/class/clan/title or reading/transmission structures, and cannot by itself establish sex, Wa/frog affiliation, or historical identity.

textual_relations.guard: Do not count as independent deities unless independent witness evidence survives collation.
佩文韵府 preserves 女蔑 while earlier Guo Pu-line text preserves 女薎; compare witnesses rather than count two gods.
Two distinct 女歧 occurrences in 天问 remain separate occurrence nodes until identity is tested.
左传 has 女艾, 经典释文 says 女如字又音汝, and 竹书纪年 tradition has 汝艾. This relation does not establish sex.
左传注疏/经典释文 and 公羊传注疏 explicitly annotate 女音汝 in multiple Spring-and-Autumn personal-name/title contexts. Do not infer that every 女 graph has this reading.

textual_relations.a: 女氏/女艾/女鸠/女方/女宽
textual_relations.guard: 张澍辑世本 attributes this lineage statement to 陆贾新语, but the passage is absent from the received 新语 and from a modern collected 新语佚文 set. Do not cite it as extant Western-Han text.
宋路史国名纪 and later philologists treat 女/汝 as a polity/clan reading in some names; this is a hypothesis to test against earlier witnesses.
Same-event overlap remains, but modern Old Chinese reconstructions do not support the traditional claim that 艾 and 歧 are close. Preserve separate occurrence nodes.
Same surface name in 天问 is not enough to merge a nine-child divine occurrence with the Shaokang-Hanjiao occurrence.
Historical spelling is 女媊; later transmission explicitly glosses 媊音前.
Textual-critical duplicate hypothesis is not raw-source identity fact.

cultural_family_guard: Wa/frog membership requires an independent evidence bundle such as western geography + water/rain/Chishui + frog/Wa phonology/iconography/ritual/genealogy. 女X form alone has zero positive weight. Multiple Spring-and-Autumn names explicitly read 女 as 汝, while Qin genealogy independently proves maternal-clan ancestry exists; reading, clan, sex, office, and cultural-family semantics must be modeled as separate fields rather than collapsed into one universal 女-prefix rule.
